questions.q: Per this lesson's definitions, what is a constraint?
options: Something the solution must do or provide for the business
A fixed boundary the design cannot change, usually imposed from outside the project
A stated, unconfirmed belief flagged so it can be revisited later
Any requirement that happens to be difficult to implement
questions.explain: A constraint is a boundary you cannot design around because it's already fixed by something outside the project's control, unlike a requirement (what the solution must do) or an assumption (an unconfirmed belief).

questions.q: Why does this lesson warn against treating an assumption as a confirmed fact?
options: Because assumptions are always wrong by definition
Because Salesforce prohibits architects from making assumptions during intake
Because a design can collapse later if an unconfirmed assumption it depended on turns out to be false
Because assumptions and requirements are legally the same thing under most contracts
questions.explain: Treating an unconfirmed assumption as settled fact is risky precisely because the design is relying on it being true — if it later turns out false, the design built on top of it is at risk.

questions.q: Which LTV Global system does this lesson identify as having no modern API and being reachable only through batch file transfer?
options: The ERP system
The financial system
The customer portal
The identity provider
questions.explain: The lesson identifies the legacy financial system specifically as the decades-old mainframe platform with no modern API, reachable only through batch file transfer — a fixed constraint, not something this project can fix.

questions.q: In the Lab scenario, the VP of Sales insists the new system must talk to the ERP 'in real time.' What is the key distinction the lesson asks you to draw out?
options: That the VP is referring to the financial system, which genuinely cannot do real time, so the statement must simply be accepted as fact
That the ERP and financial system are the same platform, so the VP's statement settles both at once
That the VP named the ERP (not the financial system), so this needs to be tested as a possible assumption rather than accepted outright as a hard constraint
That real-time integration requirements are never worth questioning during intake
questions.explain: The VP named the ERP specifically, which the lesson does not describe as having the financial system's real-time limitation — so the statement should be tested as a claim or assumption, not blurred with the financial system's actual, fixed constraint.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed in this lesson as one of LTV Global's nonfunctional requirements?
options: Dealers must be able to place parts orders online
The platform must support roughly 10,000 internal users and millions of customer records without degrading
Internal users must authenticate through the company's identity provider
A single Salesforce platform must give a 360-degree view of each customer
questions.explain: Supporting ~10,000 users and millions of records without degrading is a quality of the system (a nonfunctional requirement) as opposed to the functional requirements listed, which describe specific things the system must do.
